extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, supervisory staff, patent attorneys/agents and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling, entry, refusal, and formatting of amendments filed after a Notice of Allowance (post-allowance amendments) under 37 CFR 1.312 and related rules (37 CFR 1.121, 1.633, etc.). Covers examiner authority, supervisory approval, required statements, fees, and processing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle action / shortened reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is in condition for allowance except for formal matters; prosecution on the merits is closed in accordance with Ex parte Quayle. A shortened statutory period for reply to this action is set to expire TWO MONTHS from the mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 to issue an Ex parte Quayle action. Examiner must explain the formal matters which must be corrected in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments received after mailing of Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment, even though prepared by applicant prior to allowance, does not reach the Office until after the notice of allowance has been mailed, such amendment has the status of one filed under 37 CFR 1.312; its entry is a matter of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is filed in the Office prior to mailing but received by the examiner after mailing, it has the same standing as though the notice had not been mailed. See MPEP §§ 714.16–714.16(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 general rule — filing deadline and entry authority
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right in an application after the mailing of the notice of allowance. Any amendment filed pursuant to this section must be filed before or with the payment of the issue fee, and may be entered on the recommendation of the primary examiner, approved by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid. The Commissioner has delegated approval to supervisory patent examiners. See MPEP § 714.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of changes considered 'amendments' under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment of an application by applicant after allowance broadly encompasses any change in the file record of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) an amendment to the specification, (B) a change in the drawings, (C) an amendment to the claims, (D) a change in the inventorship, (E) the submission of prior art, etc. (text explicitly lists these examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner authority to enter formal corrections after Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance has been mailed, the application is technically no longer under the jurisdiction of the primary examiner. He or she can, however, make examiner’s amendments and has authority to enter amendments submitted after Notice of Allowance which embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification or drawing, or formal matters in a claim without changing the scope thereof, or the cancellation of claims, without forwarding to the supervisory patent examiner for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1302.04 for examiner’s amendments. Such formal corrections may be entered by the primary examiner; other types require supervisory approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments requiring supervisory patent examiner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments other than those which merely embody the correction of formal matters without changing the scope of the claims require approval by the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TC Director establishes policy for trivial informalities. Amendments that (A) are needed for proper disclosure/protection and (B) require no substantial additional work by the Office may be considered and recommended by the primary examiner for entry. Consider whether amendment reopens prosecution or requires extra work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required remarks accompanying amendments that affect disclosure/scope/add claims
rubrics_metrics.description: As to amendments affecting the disclosure, the scope of any claim, or that add a claim, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state the reasons on which reliance is placed to show specified points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remarks must state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 not to be used for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for the continued prosecution of an application after it has been passed for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending non-entry, a detailed statement is not necessary; a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and briefly why is usually adequate. Sufficient reasons include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; (C) the amendment would involve materially added work for the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and treatment of a 'clean' set of claims after Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit an entire clean set of pending claims after Notice of Allowance; entry is subject to 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the clean set makes no changes, it will be entered to make patent publication accurate. If some claims are amended in the clean set, examiner may choose not to enter under 1.312. A clean version directs cancellation of prior versions; parenthetical expressions from prior claims should not be repeated in the clean set except when a claim is being amended. A marked-up version is required only for claims being changed; examiner has no responsibility to ensure accuracy of applicant’s claim rewriting. 37 CFR 1.111(c) requirements re: pointing out patentable novelty apply to 1.312 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for additional claims added by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required. See MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after payment of the issue fee are not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the date the issue fee was paid. Use form paragraph 13.10 to notify applicant when an amendment was filed after issue fee payment and will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims received after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment received after notice of allowance includes cloned or substantially copied claims from a patent, the entry of the copied patent claims is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2305.04 for procedure and MPEP § 714.19. See MPEP § 607 and § 714.16(c) for fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with a motion under 37 CFR 1.633
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment filed with a motion under 37 CFR 1.633(c)(2) applies to an application in issue, the amendment is not entered unless and until the motion has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter amendment until motion resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and examiner recommendation for 1.312 amendments (PTO-271 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are promptly considered by the examiner who indicates whether or not its entry is recommended by writing 'Enter — 312', 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink; favorable consideration leads to entry and preparation of a Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner stamps and signs PTO-271 to indicate recommendation; form paragraph 7.85 may be used to indicate entry. If recommendation is adverse, a report giving reasons for nonentry is typed on PTO-271 and signed by primary examiner; form paragraph 7.87 may be used for nonentry. The file and papers are forwarded to the supervisory patent examiner for consideration/approval and mailing in either case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry in part under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the general rule is that an amendment should not be entered in part and refused in part, where an amendment contains multiple claims/changes some acceptable and some not, the acceptable portions should be entered and the refused portions canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should renumber claims if necessary, cancel refused claims in pencil on the amendment, and submit PTO-271 recommending entry of acceptable portion and nonentry of remainder with reasons. Applicant may be notified using form paragraph 7.86. Entry-in-part is not recommended unless the full additional fee required, if any, accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing corrections included in 37 CFR 1.312 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 1.312 amendment includes proposed drawing changes which are acceptable, the Office response should include form paragraph 6.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.48 gives applicant ONE MONTH from mailing or until expiration of the Notice of Allowance period (whichever is longer) to file corrected drawings. Use with 1.312 amendment notice when there is a drawing correction proposal or request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments concerning merely formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification, formal changes in a claim without changing scope, or cancellation of claims may be approved by the primary examiner without supervisory approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner indicates approval by writing 'Enter Formal Matters Only' and initialing. Such amendments do not require submission to supervisory examiner prior to entry. If disapproved in whole or part, supervisory signature is required. Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271) is date stamped and mailed by the TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of amendments ordinarily denied entry (list A–Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: A catalog of amendment categories that are ordinarily denied entry after final prosecution is closed or where other defects exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP lists: (A) amendments presenting an unpatentable claim or requiring a new search or raising new issues where prosecution is closed; (B) substitute specifications not complying with 37 CFR 1.125; (C) a patent claim suggested by examiner but not timely presented (absent Commissioner authorization); (D) certain copied patent claims (see MPEP § 2307.03); (E) unsigned/improperly signed amendments or signed by suspended/excluded practitioner; (F) amendments filed after statutory/set period for reply; (G) amendments so worded they cannot be entered with accuracy; (H) amendment canceling all claims and presenting no substitute; (I) amendment in application no longer within examiner’s jurisdiction except exceptions; (J) drawing amendments held to contain new matter until settled; (K) amendatory papers with objectionable remarks (37 CFR 1.3) referred to TC Director; (L) amendments not in permanent ink or on easily erasable paper; (M) amendments presenting claims in excess of number paid for without fee; (N) amendments canceling elected invention claims and presenting only nonelected invention claims (nonresponsive); (O) amendments including changes not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (no replacement paragraphs/claims); (P) preliminary amendments unduly interfering with first Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)); (Q) second/subsequent supplemental replies unduly interfering with an Office action (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)). While ordinarily denied, a subsequent showing by applicant may lead to entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where amendments are entered in part (examples A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances in which a partial entry of an amendment is appropriate to avoid record confusion or to accept non-problematic portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) substitute specification unacceptable but other amendatory matter (claims/new claims) acceptable — enter acceptable parts and deny substitute spec entry; (B) 1.312 amendment partly approved and partly disapproved — enter approved parts only; (C) where prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex parte Quayle) and amendment cures only formal defect but adds claims some of which are unpatentable or require further search — enter only formal matter; (D) amendment accompanying motion granted only in part — enter to extent motion was granted; (E) after March 1, 2001, an amendment that amends specification not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 but presents rewritten/new claims should be entered in part (deny spec changes, enter compliant claim changes). Examiner writes 'Enter' in red ink and initials left margin opposite enterable portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertently entered amendments have no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as if changes had not been legally made. If unauthorized entry is to be retained in the file, annotate the amendatory paper 'Not Officially Entered', give it a paper number, and list on the file wrapper as 'Not Entered'. See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for papers that may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments — 37 CFR 1.121 formatting rules (specification, claims, drawings, no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications are made by filing a paper directing specified amendments and must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (and §1.52). Rules cover how to present amendments to the specification, replacement sections, substitute specifications, claims, drawings, and limitations such as no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules include: (b)(1) instruction unambiguously identifying location to delete/replace/add paragraphs; supply replacement paragraph(s) in clean form and a marked-up version showing changes (brackets for deletions, underlining for additions) except added/deleted paragraphs where marked-up not required; (b)(2) replacement section procedure; (b)(3) substitute specification requires instruction, substitute spec (complying with §1.125(b)), and a marked-up version; (b)(4) deleted matter may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted matter; (c)(1) claims amended by rewriting must be in clean form and accompanied by a marked-up version on separate pages showing changes; parenthetical status (e.g., 'amended', 'new') must follow claim number and be consistent between clean and marked-up versions; (c)(2) canceled claim may be reinstated only as a new claim with new number; (c)(3) a clean version of entire claim set may be submitted but will be construed as cancellation of prior versions, and a marked-up version is required only for claims being changed; (d) drawings: changes must be submitted on separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval, and upon approval new compliant drawings (§1.84) must be filed; (e) disclosure consistency: amendment must secure substantial correspondence among claims, specification, and drawings; (f) no amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure; (g) exception for examiner’s amendments: Office-made changes may be made by specific instructions to insert/delete set forth in examiner’s amendment (compliance with certain paragraphs not required); (h)-(j) special rules for reissue, reexamination, and provisional applications respectively (e.g., reissue amendments follow §1.173; reexamination amendments follow §1.530(d)-(j); provisional amendments not normally made but if made must comply and be placed in provisional file but may not be entered). The term 'brackets' means square brackets [ ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-compliant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments and non-final amendments not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 are handled by technical support staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff notifies applicant of defects by mailing a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment. See MPEP § 714.03 for further treatment.
